samples.summary: Two of the three changed `toggleList` exits have no test asserting heading restoration
samples.evidence: The new test file only drives `editor.toggleList` (packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:209-244), i.e. the docs `editor.ts` surface. The identical change at `TextEditor.toggleList` (text-editor.ts:2166 — the Ctrl+Shift+7/8 keyboard shortcut path, reached from text-editor.ts:960/966) and at `initializeTextBox`'s `toggleList` (text-box-editor.ts:1122) is untested. The only existing text-box coverage is `expect(() => api.toggleList('unordered')).not.toThrow()` (packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:333), which passes whether or not the heading is restored. Ironically the helper's own doc comment says it exists to keep 'the three toggleList implementations ... from drifting', yet only one is regression-guarded.
searchedFor: packages/docs/test/** for text-editor test files (Glob packages/docs/test/**/*text-editor* → none)

samples.summary: The new 'headingLevel is inert on a list-item' invariant is asserted in a comment but nothing tests it (export/serialize/clipboard readers)
samples.evidence: The change introduces a genuinely new document state — a `list-item` block that carries `headingLevel` — and the `Block` doc comment claims 'every reader (export, `blockStyleId`, toolbar labels) gates on `type === 'heading'`'. No test in the diff or the suite feeds such a block to any reader. I checked markdown serialization (src/serialize/markdown.ts:103), pdf outline (src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:201), docx export (src/export/docx-exporter.ts:184), `blockStyleId` (src/model/named-styles.ts:99) and clipboard copy (`cloneBlockWithFreshIds`, text-editor.ts:3404, which copies `headingLevel` verbatim, plus paste head/tail merges at text-editor.ts:3578/3607). The new tests assert only `type`/`headingLevel` fields on the store and Doc; if any of those readers stopped gating on type, or a copied bulleted heading pasted into body text resurrected as a heading, every test in this diff would still pass.

samples.summary: No test that the toolbar's `getBlockType()` reports a bulleted heading as a plain list item
samples.evidence: `getBlockType()` returns `headingLevel: block.headingLevel` with no `type === 'heading'` gate (editor.ts:2793; same at text-box-editor.ts:1098), so a bulleted heading now reports `{type:'list-item', headingLevel:2}` where it previously reported no level. The diff's own comment lists 'toolbar labels' as a reader that gates on type. No test in list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts (or elsewhere) calls `getBlockType()` after bulleting a heading, so a wrong style-dropdown label would ship silently.

samples.summary: toggleList round-trip only exercised on a collapsed single-block selection
samples.evidence: `editor.toggleList` iterates `forEachBlockInSelection` (editor.ts:2867-2876), but all three round-trip tests set an anchor==focus caret on one block. A multi-block selection mixing a heading, a paragraph and a plain list item — where the per-block `unlistedBlockType` choice actually differs across blocks — is not covered.

I checked markdown serialization (src/serialize/markdown.ts:103), pdf outline (src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:201), docx export (src/export/docx-exporter.ts:184), `blockStyleId` (src/model/named-styles.ts:99) and clipboard copy (`cloneBlockWithFreshIds`, text-editor.ts:3404, which copies `headingLevel` verbatim, plus paste head/tail merges at text-editor.ts:3578/3607). verdict.reason: Verified the absence claim independently. The diff introduces a new document state - a list-item block retaining headingLevel (types.ts:58 comment; memory.ts:258; yorkie-doc-store.ts:1391-1395) - and the retention/restore behavior itself is well covered (list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:90-250; frontend yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1527-1546,1916-1940). But no test feeds such a block to a reader. A repo-wide multiline search (list-item within 1200 chars of headingLevel) across all test/spec files returned 10 files; I read each relevant region: blockStyleId is tested only with createBlock('list-item') with no level (model/named-styles.test.ts:17); markdown tests pair levels only with heading blocks (serialize/markdown.test.ts:74-90); the clipboard list-item test carries no headingLevel (clipboard.test.ts:66-87) and the heading test is a separate block (:44-64); the PDF fixture's three headingLevel entries are all on type heading; the toolbar readers are called only without a level (blockTypeToStyleId("list-item") at text-style-options.test.ts:37, getBlockLabel("paragraph") at :48), so the type === "heading" gates at text-style-options.ts:112,127 are never exercised with the new state. No test calls cloneBlockWithFreshIds with a bulleted heading (only table cases in paste-table-into-cell.test.ts). The plan doc (20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:24-26,46-47) states reader inertness as an assumption and scopes tests to the round trip only. I found no counterexample and no valid refutation ground: "already-guarded" would describe the production gating, not a test, and this lens's claim is about missing coverage of a newly reachable state reaching export/serialize/style-id/clipboard readers.
